intro: Florence rewards slow walkers with Renaissance art, lively markets, and river views around nearly every corner. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Tram T2 links the airport to Santa Maria Novella station and runs until about 00:30 on weekdays and 02:00 on weekends; the route takes about 20 minutes.
Tram 1 runs from Villa Constanza Park & Ride through the western suburbs to Santa Maria Novella, about 25 minutes, every 3 to 10 minutes.
AutolineeToscane buses serve the city. Tap a contactless Visa, Mastercard or Amex card, or buy a €1.70 paper ticket before boarding; a 90-minute hop-on, hop-off window applies.
Taxis have few stands and are hard to hail on the street. Book by phone or use the stand at Santa Maria Novella, and carry cash. Check locally whether Uber or FreeNow is available.
Driving inside the historic centre is restricted by camera and fines are high. Park at Park & Ride sites and walk or take the bus in.
Most of the centre is flat and walkable in about 30 minutes end to end. Shared city bikes are available, and cycle paths help you bypass the old streets.

duomo.name: Florence Cathedral
duomo.price_text: Free to enter · dome climb approx. €20–30 (check on the day)
duomo.hours: Mon–Fri about 10:00–17:00 · Sat about 10:00–16:45 · Sun limited (check on the day)
duomo.tip: Book a timed slot online for the dome climb, which has over 400 steps.

uffizi.name: Uffizi Gallery
uffizi.price_text: approx. €25 full ticket plus booking fee (check on the day)
uffizi.hours: Tue–Sun about 08:15–18:30 · Closed Mon (check on the day)
uffizi.tip: Book a timed entry online weeks ahead, because same-day tickets often sell out.

accademia.name: Galleria dell'Accademia
accademia.price_text: approx. €16–18 plus booking fee (check on the day)
accademia.hours: Tue–Sun about 08:15–18:50 · Closed Mon (check on the day)
accademia.tip: Go straight to the David gallery at the end of the hall, then see the unfinished Michelangelo sculptures.

ponte.name: Ponte Vecchio
ponte.tip: Cross at sunset for the Arno views, and look for the shops that line the bridge.

vecchio.name: Palazzo Vecchio
vecchio.price_text: approx. €17–25 depending on route (check on the day)
vecchio.hours: Daily about 09:00–19:00 · Friday until about 23:00 in some periods (check on the day)
vecchio.tip: Climb the tower for a view over the Piazza della Signoria, and see the copy of David in the square.

santacroce.name: Basilica of Santa Croce, Florence
santacroce.price_text: approx. €14–18 with museum and cloisters (check on the day)
santacroce.hours: Mon–Sat about 09:30–17:30 · Sun afternoons only (check on the day)
santacroce.tip: Visit the tombs of Galileo, Michelangelo and Machiavelli, and see Giotto's frescoes in the Bardi and Peruzzi chapels.

boboli.name: Boboli Gardens
boboli.hours: Daily from about 08:15 until sunset · Closing times vary (check on the day)
boboli.tip: Walk up to the Forte di Belvedere for one of the best views over the city.

pitti.name: Pitti Palace
pitti.price_text: approx. €16 for Palatine Gallery · combined tickets may cost more (check on the day)
pitti.hours: Tue–Sun about 08:15–18:50 · Closed Mon (check on the day)
pitti.tip: Entry is often bundled with the Boboli Gardens, so check the combined ticket first.

annunciation.name: Annunciation
annunciation.hours: Same as Uffizi Gallery (check on the day)
annunciation.tip: Look for Leonardo's early Annunciation in Room 15 of the Uffizi, not the Fra Angelico fresco in San Marco.

arno.name: Arno River
arno.tip: Walk the Lungarno embankments on either side for calm views and sunset light.

david.name: David
david.hours: Same as Galleria dell'Accademia (check on the day)
david.tip: Stand in the central gallery for the full view, and book a timed slot to avoid long queues.

primavera.name: Primavera
primavera.hours: Same as Uffizi Gallery (check on the day)
primavera.tip: Find Botticelli's Primavera in the Botticelli rooms, and allow time for the crowd around it.

venus.name: The Birth of Venus
venus.hours: Same as Uffizi Gallery (check on the day)
venus.tip: Look for Botticelli's Birth of Venus in the same rooms as Primavera, and go early to get a clear view.

mercato.name: Mercato Centrale
mercato.price_text: Food costs vary by stall (check on the day)
mercato.tip: Eat at the upstairs food court for stalls such as the lampredotto or sandwich counters.

michelangelo.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
michelangelo.tip: Go up at sunset for the classic view over the Duomo and the Arno, and bring a light jacket.

oltrarno.name: Oltrarno neighbourhood walk
oltrarno.price_text: Free to walk · workshop or tour costs vary
oltrarno.hours: Shops open about 10:00–19:00 · many close on Sunday (check on the day)
oltrarno.tip: Wander the artisan workshops on Via Maggio and Borgo San Frediano for a local feel.

foodtour.name: Florence food and wine tour
foodtour.price_text: approx. €70–110 per person (check on the day)
foodtour.tip: Choose a small group tour with tastings of Tuscan wine and cured meats, and check that the tasting is included.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: The Uffizi, Accademia and Michelangelo's David, with gallery days you can plan in advance.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Tuscan markets, trattorias and wine bars on a walkable centre.

styles.label: Romance
styles.blurb: Riverside walks, hilltop views and quiet dinners after the crowds leave.

stays.why: Near the main station, the Duomo area and the tram links to the airport and Park & Ride sites.
Close to the Medici Chapels and the central market; busy streets with many restaurants.
Lively piazza, leather shops and easy walks to the Duomo and the Arno; good for food.
Quieter artisan streets across the Arno, with Palazzo Pitti and Santo Spirito square nearby.

food: Eat at a trattoria with a handwritten menu; Florentine dishes like ribollita and bistecca are best shared.
Visit the Mercato Centrale for a casual lunch; the San Lorenzo market stalls are good for snacks.
Try a schiacciata sandwich or a gelato from a shop with covered tubs and no piled-high colours.
Book dinner ahead on weekends and in high season; many places close one day a week, so check first.
Aperitivo is common in the late afternoon; order a spritz and small snacks at a bar.
Tap water is safe to drink; ask for a bottle of local Chianti at a wine bar for a fair price.
more_time: Take a day trip to Siena or Pisa by train or bus; check timetables on the day.
Spend a half day in the Chianti hills by taxi or organised tour; book ahead in high season.
Add a second night for a slower pace, with a cooking class or a Uffizi and Boboli Gardens day.
